To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the public's conception of alcoholism is a complex one that is not reducible to a simple medical model.

the public's conception of alcoholism and of the deviant drinker has been changing in the direction of the medical model, and that the medical model has been increasingly adopted as a frame of reference for the public's understanding of the problem of alcoholism.

the deviant drinker is a deviant because he drinks in a manner that is not acceptable in his reference group, and the deviant drinkers in our sample did not differ significantly from the nondeviant drinkers in their attitudes toward alcoholism and alcoholics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social construction of the alcoholic and the deviant drinker.
the extent to which the deviant drinker is perceived as a sick person by the general public and by the alcoholic himself.
the social definition of deviant drinking and the role of this definition in the social control of the deviant drinker.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a strong tendency in the United States for the public to view alcoholism as a disease, but there is a tendency toward the view of alcoholism as a criminal offense.
the public has become increasingly aware that the deviant drinker is a sick person.
the deviant drinker is a medical patient, not a criminal, who is suffering from a disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been successful in changing the public image of the alcoholic and the deviant drinker from a person who is a social misfit to one who is a sick person.
the public has been educated in recent years to believe that alcoholism is a disease.
we have been trying to change public opinion regarding the causes of alcoholism and to make people aware of the fact that alcoholism is not a crime but a disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public is not as well informed about alcoholism and its causes as we would like it to be.
there is a lot of room for improvement in the way that we think about alcohol use, alcohol use disorders and alcohol-related problems.
